overview: This one-page file consists of a list-of-papers or cross-reference entry concerning anthropology, ethnology, ethnography, and archaeology in Japan. It records Joseph C. Grew’s despatch no. 1929 from Japan, dated July 3, reporting that Tokyo Imperial University would commemorate Harvard University’s tercentenary by presenting it with a collection of Japanese archaeological specimens; the OCR’s “Mayyard University” is an evident misreading of Harvard University. The entry directs researchers to a separately filed Harvard University subject file rather than preserving the despatch itself.

people.name: Joseph C. Grew
people.role: Sender of the referenced despatch; U.S. Ambassador to Japan

subfiles.title: List-of-papers entry for Grew despatch no. 1929 on archaeological specimens
subfiles.about: The entry cross-references a despatch reporting Tokyo Imperial University’s planned gift of Japanese archaeological specimens to Harvard University for its tercentenary.
subfiles.summary: This filing sheet identifies despatch no. 1929 from Joseph C. Grew, dated July 3. The despatch reported that Tokyo Imperial University would present Harvard University with a collection of Japanese archaeological specimens to commemorate Harvard’s tercentenary. The entry redirects the reader to file 093.941—Harvard University/1, indicating that the substantive document was filed elsewhere. The year 1936 is inferred from Harvard’s tercentenary.

interest: The sheet is useful as evidence of scholarly and cultural exchange between Japanese and American universities during the interwar period, particularly the circulation of archaeological collections as commemorative gifts. It also reveals State Department filing practice: material relevant to Japanese archaeology was removed or cross-referenced to an institutional file on Harvard University. Although the underlying despatch is absent, its number, sender, date, subject, and alternate file location provide a precise trail for further archival research.
